AI companies are now global by default.

The 100 largest AI companies on Stripe by revenue reached an average of 120 markets by their third year of operation. Collectively, they now draw 48% of revenue from outside their home markets.

But global availability is only the first step. Our latest analysis looks at where AI demand is growing fastest—and what it takes to turn that demand into durable revenue.

A few findings stood out: 

🇰🇷 South Korea stood out as an already-large market that continues to grow quickly at 134% year-over-year. 

🇲🇽 Mexico emerged as a breakout market, with 264% year over year growth despite its current smaller size.  

💳 The fastest-growing AI companies use 2x more local payment methods than the broader cohort, underscoring that localization matters as much as reach.

For AI businesses, the opportunity is not simply to sell in more countries. It is to build experiences that let customers in those markets buy in the ways that work best for them.

After seven extraordinary years building Stripe's go-to-market engine, I'm stepping into a new role: Vice Chair of Stripe. As Vice Chair, I'll represent the company with business, government, and policy leaders around the world, alongside Patrick Collison and John Collison. 

The internet economy is at an inflection point. Governments, regulators, and multilateral bodies are making once-in-a-generation decisions about how digital commerce is regulated and enabled—decisions that will set the operating conditions for entrepreneurs for decades. Stripe serves millions of businesses in nearly every country on earth. We have both the standing and the responsibility to shape those decisions. That's what I'll be doing: engaging heads of government, trade bodies, and global business leaders to advocate for decisions that advance entrepreneurship and increase the economic dynamism that too many parts of the world have been starved of.

I've spent the last 25 years of my career building things, teams, markets, relationships. This next chapter is about using all of that on behalf of the businesses that trust Stripe to power their growth. 

As I start this new role, I'm delighted to have Tyler Bryson take over as Stripe's Chief Revenue Officer. Tyler brings two decades of experience building, scaling, and leading revenue-generating teams and has had a tremendous impact leading our Americas business. He knows our customers, understands what they need and we’re all very excited for his leadership as Stripe’s CRO.

We've already issued nearly 135,000 Krak Cards across the UK and EEA this year.

Today, I’m excited to announce my book, Built to Grow: A Handbook for High-Performance Sales Teams, is available for pre-order with Stripe Press!

I’ve been doing sales since I was a teenager, starting with selling flowers in a flower shop and toys at international trade shows. And for the last twenty years, I have helped build and run enterprise sales teams at software startups.

The startups where I’ve worked were usually run by technical founders who didn’t have much sales experience, so when it came time to build their GTM organization, I found they often asked the same questions: How do I hire my first sales person? How do I figure out which customer to sell to? How do you run a pipeline meeting? How do I build a repeatable sales motion? What is a sales playbook? And how do I make sure my sales team hits their revenue targets?

10 years ago I started advising founders and I found myself looking for books to recommend. I was surprised I couldn’t find a practical handbook that answered the questions I heard most often.  So, I wrote Built To Grow.

I poured everything I know into this book. It’s the handbook I wished I’d had: a systematic framework for founders setting out to hire their first sales team and build a predictable, reliable revenue engine. 

Hopefully, you’ll find it helpful!

posts.content:
Businesses often tell me they believe the best way to fight a “product not received” dispute is to submit more evidence. We analyzed one million “product not received” disputes on Stripe and found that evidence specificity matters more than volume.

For physical goods, delivery information was the strongest signal we studied. Businesses that submitted delivery confirmation, a GPS delivery map, and a recipient signature saw a 44 percentage point higher win rate than businesses that did not submit these types of evidence.

The same lesson applies to digital goods: disputes that had activity logs that showed that a customer accessed or used the specific product saw a 10 percentage point higher win rate than disputes without them.

Smart Disputes is designed to apply these best practices for you, helping you save time and recover revenue. It uses AI to automatically assemble tailored evidence packets for eligible card disputes so you don’t have to manually implement them dispute by dispute.

Read the analysis: https://lnkd.in/gQrBZTiN.

AgentCore payments is now generally available, as part of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, built with Coinbase and Stripe.

An agent's autonomy has always ended where payment began. It could reason, plan, and choose the right tool, then a paid article or API would stop the task and send it back to a person.

Now the task keeps going. The agent buys the article it needs, pays for API access, pays for the MCP server it calls. The payment resolves inside the execution loop.

Every transaction runs in a payment session with a spend cap and an expiry, checked deterministically at the infrastructure layer, with audit trails in AgentCore observability. Support for both x402 and MPP means you integrate once and your agent can pay any compatible service, whichever protocol the merchant uses.

A new level of agent autonomy is unlocked. https://go.aws/45vrJQt

Last week, agent traffic surpassed human traffic on the internet for the first time. Agents browsing webpages account for some of that traffic, but our data points to a more significant reason for this growth: agents building software.

Agent traffic to our documentation grew more than 10x in 2025 and now makes up nearly 40% of docs traffic. We’ve also seen exponential growth in new Stripe CLI users over the past year, with 70% of CLI requests for API resources coming from agents.

Our data shows that agents are now fully capable of independently writing code and integrating with APIs like Stripe’s. And yet, many of the steps adjacent to writing code—such as provisioning infrastructure, managing credentials, setting up accounts, and connecting services together—are still too hard for agents to do on their own.

We've added more platforms on Stripe in the last 3 months than we did in the last 6 months of 2025. New platform businesses on Stripe are up 106% year over year. And, fascinatingly, that growth rate is still accelerating.

A few things stand out to me:
1. These are real businesses onboarding real users with real volume. We did a deep audit of our newest platforms (manual reviews, LLM classification, heuristic checks) and they're legit. Even better, our January 2026 cohort is hitting $1M in volume at a higher rate than any previous cohort. 

2. AI is changing how developers build on Stripe, with 42% of new integrations involving some form of AI assistance. For Connect users, we're leaning into this trend heavily with better docs, blueprints, and agent-friendly tooling. We recently added a new connect-recommend skill to the official Stripe plugin for Claude, available to users who install or invoke the plugin. This skill provides agent-steering resources that help AI recommend the Connect integration for the use case. In Claude skill evals, the rewritten Connect guidance improved the pass rate from ~40% to ~90% across our six core Connect scenarios.

3. The macro tailwinds are real and, at the same time, we've also shipped a ton of improvements to onboarding and integration flows that are compounding. Users building “complete” integrations (a leading indicator for us) is up 200% YoY.

For SaaS platforms thinking about embedded payments or financial services, the barrier to entry has never been lower. The platforms building now are scaling faster than we've ever seen.

So excited for what’s happening with the segment and we want your feedback. If you're a platform founder or leader, would love to hear what's top of mind for you right now.
